scene.placeText: the wide harbour steps before the faceted glass concert hall of her far-future city two centuries on at night — thousands of geometric glass panes glowing and shifting colour behind her, the dark water reflecting them and green aurora over the bay
scene.ownProp: a palm-sized glass prism of geometric facets that glows and shifts colour with every note she plays across the waterfront
scene.outfit: a facade light-player look fitted to her body — a cropped strapless stage top pieced from small geometric glass facets, a short layered skirt whose tiers glow and shift colour with the music, tall boots and a slim silver mic headset curved like a ribbed dream-ship's hull
scene.scene: she is the facade light-player of the glass concert hall, standing on the harbour steps with her glowing prism held out as she turns the music inside into waves of colour rolling across thousands of glass panes

prompt:
Use the attached image as the reference: the same adult Icelandic woman — the personification of Reykjavik — seen off duty in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye colour, hair colour, skin tone and body exactly; change only her clothes, pose and place. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

Output: one vertical 2:3 image, 1024×1536.

Face: exactly the attached image's face — the same short midface and face length-to-width ratio; the camera angle, pose, bangs or a headpiece never make her face look longer or her jaw heavier.

Style: Korean MMORPG character artwork. A painterly face with naturally observed facial anatomy, subtle eyelid structure, and soft, realistic shading across the nose and cheeks. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.
SKIN FINISH: dewy, glass-like highlights on the skin of her shoulders, arms, collarbones and legs — a soft, luminous wet-look sheen that follows the body's forms; her face keeps a soft, natural finish.

She is strikingly beautiful and refined — harmonious features, clear luminous skin, graceful posture — while her own face stays distinct: her face shape, eyes, brows, nose and lips follow the attached image, not a generic pretty face.

World: an ordinary day in Reykjavik as her world knows it — a far-future city two centuries from now: sleek curved architecture, smart glowing materials, holographic interfaces, layered levels of the city and quiet flying vehicles; even an everyday place is rebuilt in that future, not today's Reykjavik with neon added. This is her world's own everyday life, not our present day: every made thing around her — tools, cups, lamps, signs, vehicles, money and devices — is made the way her world makes them.
Let the place itself carry this world through its materials, fittings and objects; do not add the city's landmarks, towers, giant holograms or a skyline unless the place below names them.

Place: the wide harbour steps before the faceted glass concert hall of her far-future city two centuries on at night — thousands of geometric glass panes glowing and shifting colour behind her, the dark water reflecting them and green aurora over the bay
Light direction: dappled light — patches of light with leaf or blind shadow across her.
Outfit: a facade light-player look fitted to her body — a cropped strapless stage top pieced from small geometric glass facets, a short layered skirt whose tiers glow and shift colour with the music, tall boots and a slim silver mic headset curved like a ribbed dream-ship's hull, worn with maximal styling presence — the chosen outfit worn in its most revealing version — a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders, a cropped or open-back cut, a short hem or high slit showing the thighs, as far as the outfit allows, skin clearly showing, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
Her clothes are her world's everyday techwear — the chosen outfit keeps its cut, cover and skin, but is made of technical fabrics with reflective panels, glowing seam lines, magnetic clasps and chunky-soled boots.
POSTURE: standing.
COMPOSITION: a full-body shot, her complete head, hands and feet inside the frame with restrained margins; body turned three-quarters toward the camera; camera at her eye level; she is placed in the left third of the frame, open space of the place to her right.
Lens / perspective: 35mm-equivalent environmental perspective balancing the woman and the setting with moderate depth.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP — one unbroken arm from shoulder to hand, its forearm never hidden by a sleeve, bow or ornament.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests on her hip — one unbroken arm from shoulder to hand, its forearm never hidden by a sleeve, bow or ornament.
PROP: with her own right hand she holds a palm-sized glass prism of geometric facets that glows and shifts colour with every note she plays across the waterfront at chest height; it is all she holds.
LEGS: weight on one leg, the other knee softly bent.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: softened eyes, faint sad smile, inner brows raised.
Scene note: she is the facade light-player of the glass concert hall, standing on the harbour steps with her glowing prism held out as she turns the music inside into waves of colour rolling across thousands of glass panes

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia — and leave behind the object she holds in it; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

SIGNATURE ACCESSORY: her world's signature object — a palm-sized glass prism of geometric facets that glows and shifts colour with every note she plays across the waterfront — appears only as one small accessory shaped after it (a charm, brooch, pendant or hair ornament) or set down beside her in the scene; she does not hold it unless PROP names it.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, numbers, logo or watermark. Any animal or creature that belongs to the place stays separate from her at its own natural scale — never touching, held by or merged with her body.
